 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Mirra Andreeva began her 2026 WTA Finals campaign on the back of Jessica Pegula making certain controversial remarks about her. However, the 19-year-old from Russia has so far been thoroughly impressive in her debut appearance at the prestigious year-end championships.
 First up, Andreeva clinically dispatched Elina Svitolina and in her second Round Robin phase outing, she stunned former No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka. Several fans have subsequently opined that Pegula's comments have motivated Andreeva to a great degree.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ahead of the tournament, Pegula was heard calling Andreeva a "diva" and saying that the youngster "needs to be humbled" during a practice session. Andreeva, seemingly unaffected by the American WTA veteran's comments, has been in rampant form. After getting her campaign underway with a 6-4, 6-0 victory over Svitolina, she defeated Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 on Wednesday, Nov. 11.
 Remarkably, Andreeva trailed the Belarusian 1-4 in the first set but produced a breathtaking performance afterward to take the next 11 games in succession, winning 45 of the final 55 points. The result also ensured the reigning Roland Garros champion's progress to the semifinals — a fine run already considering it's her first ever appearance at the tournament.
 On X, tennis journalist Bastien Fachan suggested that Pegula's remarks have triggered Andreeva to prove her doubters wrong at the 2026 WTA Finals:
 "Jessica Pegula has created a monster"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mirra Andreeva candidly rates her performance against Aryna Sabalenka at WTA Finals 2026
 After the match, Andreeva gave herself an eight-out-of-ten rating in terms of how well she played against the former No. 1 and four-time Major singles champion. The youngster said :
 "I would give myself a good eight. To earn a 10, you have to play the best match of your life. I feel like it was good, solid, but not great enough for a 10."
 The result also marked the first time that a player registered two 6-0 set wins in her first two outings at the WTA Finals. Up next for Andreeva is her final Round Robin phase clash with Karolina Muchova of Czechia. Muchova lost her opening match in straight sets to Sabalenka and then fell to Svitolina, with her 0-2 record mathematically ruling her out of a last-four appearance.
